description: This Bank of England page gathers the UK's approach to the operational resilience of banks and financial services firms: the ability to prevent, adapt to, respond to, recover from and learn from disruptions. It links the Prudential Regulation Authority's policy on operational resilience and its requirements for reporting operational incidents and material third-party arrangements, the work of the Cross Market Operational Resilience Group on sector-wide incident response, the CQUEST cyber questionnaire with system-level outputs for download, and the findings of the 2022 cyber stress test, after which the Financial Policy Committee updated its impact tolerance for payments and settlements in March 2023. It is maintained by the Bank of England with its Prudential Regulation Authority, working with HM Treasury and the Financial Conduct Authority. Coverage is the United Kingdom. The pages and documents are free online; no licence is stated on the page read. Caveats: it is a policy hub, not a dataset, and firm-level incident reports are confidential, so only aggregate outputs are published. For simulation it defines impact tolerances and incident categories that can set recovery targets in scenarios of cyber attacks and outages in payment and settlement systems. It is related to the BaFin DORA ICT incident analysis case study record in this catalogue.
